subject: swampTroll
pitch:
Category: Monster.
Subject: swamp troll with tusks, mohawk and bone fetishes.
Style: Blizzard/Warcraft.
reasoning:
I'm sketching out a compact but detailed Warcraft-style swamp troll design: hunched posture, long arms, tusks, a bladed mohawk crest, bone and skull fetishes, teal-green mottled skin, standing around 2.4 meters tall.

Now I'm working out the skeleton hierarchy—hips, spine chain curving forward into chest, neck, and head—and figuring out which SDK imports and chain-building calls I'll need to construct it correctly with the available builder API.

Then I'm defining the body loft stations along the spine bone: pelvis, belly, chest, and shoulders with widths and heights at each point, making sure the spine path curve roughly matches these station positions.

For the head, I'm adding a neck chain with three points producing two spans ending in a "head" joint, using world-space coordinates throughout to avoid confusion with local axes, and attaching head parts directly to that bone.

Now I'm placing a jaw joint with aim direction for the mouth hinge, then sculpting the skull as a scaled sphere with a heavy brow and small cranium, plus a wide protruding lower jaw frustum shape with tusks sticking upward -- classic troll proportions.

Placing the eyes with small protruding spheres and a brow ridge above, then working out the eye texture as a decal with yellow coloring, a dark slit pupil, and a rim outline rather than relying on glow effects.

I'll pull in the glow kit for the eyes and crystal spheres, applying it directly to the decal part since it should still work as a textured standard material. For the ears, I'm shaping long pointed troll-ear outlines that sweep back and up, extruding them outward from the skull with a thin profile.

Now I'm planning the mohawk crest as a series of spiked blades following a curved path from the top of the skull down the neck, using extruded leaf-shaped outlines placed along a catmull spline with varying heights.

Still defining the blade shape...

Still checking the polygon geometry...

Now I'm adding small gold ring bands around the tusks using short torus sweeps, then moving on to the arms—placing shoulders and using a limb function to bend elbows outward with fists positioned near the knees.

I'll give each arm a tapered sweep radius with skin coloring, then build the hand as a clawed fist: a scaled sphere with three small dark knuckle spikes angled forward-down. I'm also considering adding a bone-and-leather shoulder pad fetish piece, maybe a lathe-dome with spikes plus a bump sphere at the shoulder joint.

Now working out the troll legs: digitigrade stance with hip, ankle, and sole segments, computing thigh/shin/foot lengths and checking that the hip-to-heel distance fits within the limb's total reach.

I'm defining the leg chain with four joints and tapering radii, then adding foot sweeps with a toe box and claw spikes, checking the sole height stays near ground level. For the loincloth I'm extruding trapezoid cloth panels hanging front and back from the belt, keeping them thin and symmetric.

Now I'm working through how to texture the cloth—considering double-sided cards versus simple front/back planes positioned against the pelvis, deciding on placement and tilt to match the hip geometry before settling on a thin textured box instead.

So front cloth tilts -6 degrees, back cloth +6 degrees. Now I'm figuring out the belt geometry—sweeping a loop around the hips joint with an upward direction vector, positioned near the pelvis, using a leather-colored tube radius and checking which bone should drive its weighting.

Now I'm thinking through fetish adornments: necklaces draped as a V-shape around the neck and chest, with hanging items like skulls, bones, feathers, and teeth. I'm planning a skull helper that builds a scaled sphere with dark eye-socket spheres and a jaw box, oriented forward and attached to the chest bone.

I'm also sketching bone shapes as capsules with knob spheres at each end, feather cards for texture, and spike shapes for teeth. For the necklace strand, I'm working out a draped catmull path that hugs the chest surface, figuring out how the loft's depth and normal direction translate to actual front-facing coordinates around the neck and chest.

Since exact surface math is uncertain, I'm relying on the drape function to snap points to the nearest surface, then lifting them slightly outward, and sweeping a thin cord along that path. Finally I'm placing hanging pendants along the draped path, like positioning a skull pendant just below each anchor point.

Now I'm adding more trinkets—a skull shoulder pad, bone hangings from the belt, feathers at the mohawk base, bone bracers, and tusk rings—then deciding on the swamp troll's skin tones: a teal-blue base with darker mottling and a lighter countershaded belly.

Writing skin paint function...

Still defining spine stations...

Now I'm sketching the neck path curving from the spine tip up to the head, with tapering sweep radii, then placing the skull sphere center and radii to cap it off.

For the face, I'm positioning a brow ridge box slightly tilted, eye decals nestled under the brow following the skull's curvature, an upper jaw muzzle box tapering forward, and a small nose bump sphere at the tip.

I'm adding dark nostrils and a large curved troll nose swept as a bezier tube in dark teal, then defining the lower jaw joint and a frustum-shaped jaw box that protrudes into a chin, with tusks emerging from the jaw base angled up and outward past the upper lip, sized to clear the muzzle width.

Now I'm adjusting the upper and lower box positions so the mouth gap sits correctly, adding a dark interior box for the mouth cavity, and placing a row of small white-yellow cone teeth along the lower jaw front.

I'm skipping a beard/dreadlocks idea and instead designing the troll's long swept-back ears using an outline extrusion that curves outward and backward with a sharp point, checking the polygon points stay valid.

Adding a small gold ring torus at the ear base as a pierced accent, then working out a catmull path across the top of the skull for a mohawk crest, fitting its curve to the skull's surface using an elliptical equation so the blade bases sit flush against the head.

Continuing the spine path down to the shoulders, I'm sizing the blades to taper from tall near the head to shorter along the back, assigning each blade to the nearest bone (head versus spine joint) so they deform properly when rigged, and setting up their extrusion orientation along the body's surface.

Now I'm placing the hump geometry on the upper spine and defining the shoulder spheres and their attached arm limbs, working out joint positions, bone lengths versus reach distance, and the elbow bend direction to give the troll a slouchy, arms-back posture.

Arms hang slightly away from the body, and I'm building the hands next: a fisted sphere offset below the wrist target, with curled finger capsules arcing from knuckle to fingertip plus a thumb, all parented to the hand bone.

Now I'm figuring out wrist bracers — placing a torus along the forearm using its direction vector, positioned about three-quarters down toward the hand, with the radius sized to match the forearm's thickness there.

For feet, I'm adding toe claws as small capsules extending forward from the ankle joint, spaced at different x-offsets to form three toes, plus spike claws at the tips. Then I'm scattering small warty nubs/cones across the body surface using a loft-based scatter function.

Now I'm figuring out the loincloth: a cloth texture with a dark red base, zig-zag trim, and skull emblem, sized to drape front and back between the legs and belt area, positioning it relative to the pelvis, hip, and thigh geometry.

Placing the belt buckle as a skull plaque anchored to the belt's front surface point, then working out hanging bone decorations off the sides of the belt near the hips using capsule shapes with knobbed ends, and considering feather card accents near the mohawk base and tusk.

Now I'm adding dangling feather cards at the belt sides with upward-facing frames and forward flow, plus a tribal war paint decal across the chest using a loft surface target with white and ochre stripe patterns.

Face paint stripes get added via decals on the skull part directly, since it accepts a Part as a surface target. I'm also defining the material palette for bone, aging knobs, gold, leather, and cord, then starting a skull fetish helper function that builds a sphere-based skull shape with bone coloring.

Adding eyes and jaw details...

For the back, I want a diagonal totem staff with a skull mounted on top and feathers hanging, positioned to give a strong silhouette.

Now I'm working out the eye glow decal using an SVG design with a radial yellow-orange iris, slit pupil, and transparent background so it reads properly on the skull sphere, plus starting on a facepaint texture.

Then I'm checking the geometry for the cheek stripe decals, computing where the skull sphere's surface sits at that position so the decal lands correctly without getting hidden by the muzzle box, and adjusting the placement higher and further back to avoid overlap.

Now I'm planning the overall build order: joints first (hips root, spine chain, neck chain, legs, arms, jaw), then body mesh construction. For the neck I'm setting up a three-joint chain ending in the head, using a helper function for part placement with position, bone, rotation, and scale options, and standard sphere geometry for joints.

For the legs, I'm computing hip, knee, and heel positions per side and checking that the distances between joints stay within the allowed limb span before building the leg chain with named joints.

Now working out the arm limb geometry: shoulder root and hand target positions, checking the distance against the segment lengths to see how much bend occurs, then setting up the chain with shoulder/elbow/hand joints and a thickness sweep that's heavier at the shoulder, with a fist shape at the hand tip. Moving on to positioning fingers at the hand target.

Writing bone helper and skull functions...

Adding tusks as curved bezier sweeps from jaw base up and outward, tapering with a point cap, tuned so they clear the muzzle width.

I'm placing a gold torus band around each tusk at a point along its tangent, oriented in the XY plane so it rings the tusk naturally. Now I'm starting to write the actual build code, setting up the troll builder, paints, and spine-based bones for parts like the hump and chest attachments.

Shifting to the necklace: I'm draping a loft surface along a catmull path, sweeping a cord geometry around it, then scattering pendants along that draped path—placing a skull at the center pendant and teeth or bone shapes at the others, tracking position with a counter since the callback doesn't expose an index directly.

Writing pendant placement code...

Then I'm sketching out feathers for the totem using card frames oriented along an up vector with a forward flow direction, so they read properly from front and back, varying shading by frame axis and anchoring them to the chest bone before writing the final rich version of everything.

For the feet, I'm painting the skin and mud zones based on height along the leg, then adding a foot-pad using a tapered box shape from heel to toe, anchored at the ankle joint with a flat bottom and slightly varying width for a natural stance.

For the brows, I'm using angled capsule shapes per side with the inner end lower than the outer to give an angry slant, placing eye glow decals just below. Now I'm moving on to actually writing the code for these pieces.
